2.05.betting_forecast: 100/30 Fever Dream, 5/1 Busty Boy, 13/2 Express Surprise, 7/1 El Granjero, Stratagem, 8/1 Upfordebate, 9/1 President Scottie,
2.05.spotlight_verdict: If the ground is approaching good then Fever Dream (second choice) could take some beating as he looked well ahead of his mark at Warwick. Stablemates Express Surprise and El Granjero should put up bold shows but a chance is taken on Irish raider BRANDT. This season hasn't gone so well as the last, but the signs were more encouraging on his return to fences last time and he might be staying on stronger than a good few of his rivals.[Alistair Jones]

3.47.betting_forecast: 3/1 The Dog Thief, 7/2 Letterston Lily, 9/2 Jack Hyde, 7/1 Go Dante, Serious Operator, 11/1 Flying Fortune, 12/1 Bold Light, 14/1
3.47.spotlight_verdict: Jack Hyde (second choice) rates a solid contender, while Go Dante is a potential class act in this grade, but promising 6yo THE DOG THIEF (nap) stands out as a progressive sort in this line-up. He couldn't go with He's On Fire on his Carlisle hurdle debut but that one has strolled home in a Grade 2 at Fairyhouse since and a subsequent defeat of two next-time-out scorers at Market Rasen suggests an opening mark of 116 could prove lenient. Letterston Lily won yesterday but now has a penalty.[Andrew Sheret]

4.25.betting_forecast: 13/8 Mr Jukebox, 5/1 Berkenshtaaap, 9/1 King Kodiak, The Coffey Boy, Walk On Son, 10/1 Valette, 11/1 Velvet Vulcan, Zephlyn,
4.25.spotlight_verdict: If MR JUKEBOX is in anything like the same form as when winning readily on last week's Exeter handicap debut he'll stand a good chance of defying a 7lb penalty. Although Berkenshtaaap (second choice) failed to improve when fourth on his handicap debut he remains with unexposed potential for a leading stable which enjoys lots of success at Perth. The shortlist is completed by King Kodiak, who did too much too soon last time. [Andrew Sheret]

5.35.betting_forecast: 9/4 Rock On Ronnie, 5/2 Kill Vanhowe, 4/1 Ar Ais Aris, 5/1 Shane's Spirit, 7/1 Ksar D'Oudairies, 12/1 Fiskardo, 33/1 Cockle Bay
5.35.spotlight_verdict: When runner-up in an Irish point AR AIS ARIS finished ahead of Merry Away who was fourth in the recent Grade 2 bumper at Aintree. Rock On Ronnie edges second preference over Kill Vanhowe who was beaten by an outsider at Cork. Ksar d'Oudairies could be the pick of Mickey Bowen's two runners, both of whom are returning from lengthy absences.[Alistair Jones]
